Flutter's docs sum up the layout rule in one line:
constraints go down, sizes go up, parent sets position.
Layout is a single pass down the tree and back up:

items.text: from its parent: four numbers, a minimum and maximum width and a minimum and maximum height.
It tells each child what constraints that child gets, which can differ per child, and asks what size it wants to be.
It positions each child. A child never decides its own position.
It reports its own size to its parent, inside the constraints it was given.

content.text: So a widget can choose its size only within what its parent allows. The docs put it bluntly: a widget usually can't have any size it wants.
